claims: The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is 322 feet tall.
The Artemis II mission utilizes NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to propel four astronauts around the Moon and back.
The Space Launch System (SLS) is the most powerful operational rocket.
The Space Launch System (SLS) generates over 8 million pounds of thrust.
The Space Launch System (SLS) sends the Orion capsule on a 10-day test flight.
The Space Launch System (SLS) produces more than 8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
Artemis II is the first crewed flight to test SLS and Orion systems in deep space.
Artemis II performs a free-return trajectory around the Moon.
The launch vehicle for Artemis II is the Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1.
The Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1 consists of two solid rocket boosters and four RS-25 engines.
The crew of Artemis II includes NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch.
The crew of Artemis II includes CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
Artemis II launched from Kennedy Space Center Complex 39B in Florida.
Artemis II carries the crew into a high Earth orbit before initiating a lunar flyby.
The SLS lifts off using two solid boosters.
The two solid boosters provide over 75% of the initial power.
The solid boosters separate from the core stage shortly after launch.
The main core stage separates.
The Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) maneuvers the Orion capsule toward the Moon.
The Orion capsule separates from the rocket's upper stage once in space.
The Artemis II rocket features a mix of new and historically used hardware.
The four RS-25 engines of the Artemis II rocket were previously used on several Space Shuttle missions.
Artemis II serves as the final test before future Artemis missions land astronauts on the lunar surface.
